stories.title: The Creation
stories.summary: God creates the heavens, the earth, and living creatures over six days. The account ends with God resting on the seventh day. Light and darkness, sky and sea, dry ground and plants appear in sequence. The sun, moon and stars mark days and seasons; waters, skies and land receive living creatures. Humanity is made in God's image, male and female, and is given responsibility for the other creatures. God blesses the seventh day and sets it apart after the work of creation.

stories.title: The Fall of Man
stories.summary: The serpent persuades the woman to eat from the forbidden tree, and the man also eats. God confronts them, announces consequences, and sends them out of Eden. The serpent challenges the warning about the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. After eating, the pair recognize their nakedness, make coverings and hide. Each is questioned, and the man and woman shift responsibility. The account describes pain, difficult labor and mortality. God clothes them before placing cherubim and a flaming sword at the garden's entrance to guard the tree of life.

stories.title: Cain and Abel
stories.summary: Cain kills his brother Abel. God confronts Cain and sends him away from the ground he cultivated. Abel keeps sheep, while Cain works the soil. Their offerings receive different responses, and God warns Cain about sin before the killing. Asked where his brother is, Cain denies responsibility. Abel's blood is said to cry from the ground. Cain fears being killed as a wanderer, but God gives him a protective mark before he settles east of Eden.

stories.title: The Line of Seth
stories.summary: The genealogy traces the line from Adam through Seth to Noah. Enoch walks with God, and Noah is introduced with his three sons. After Abel's death, Eve bears Seth, and the account names Seth's son Enos. A sequence of fathers, sons, ages and deaths follows. Enoch's entry differs: he walks with God and is taken by God. Lamech names Noah in the hope of comfort from the toil of the cursed ground. The genealogy ends by naming Shem, Ham and Japheth.

stories.title: Noah and the Flood
stories.summary: Noah builds an ark to preserve his household and animals through the flood. Afterward, God establishes a covenant with Noah and living creatures, with the rainbow as its sign. The earth is described as corrupt and filled with violence. Noah follows instructions for the ark and enters with his family and animals. Rain and rising waters cover the land; later, Noah sends birds to seek signs of dry ground. He leaves the ark and builds an altar. God's covenant promises that a flood will not again destroy all flesh, and sets the bow in the clouds as its reminder.

stories.title: The Family of Noah
stories.summary: Noah’s sons and their descendants are named after the flood. The genealogy describes peoples, languages, and lands. The account first describes Noah planting a vineyard, becoming drunk and lying uncovered. Ham sees him; Shem and Japheth cover their father without looking. Noah's words concerning Canaan, Shem and Japheth follow. The next chapter traces the families of the three sons, including Nimrod and the cities connected with him. It presents the descendants spreading into distinct nations, territories and languages.

stories.title: The Tower of Babel
stories.summary: People build a city and tower to make a name for themselves and avoid being scattered. God confuses their language and scatters them across the earth. The builders settle in the plain of Shinar and use brick and mortar for a tower intended to reach heaven. Their shared language enables the project. God comes down to see the city and tower, then confuses their speech so that they cannot understand one another. Building stops, and the people are dispersed. The narrative connects the name Babel with that confusion of language.

stories.title: The Call of Abram
stories.summary: Abram’s family leaves Ur for Haran. God calls Abram to another land, and he travels to Canaan with Sarai and Lot. Terah takes Abram, Sarai and Lot from Ur toward Canaan, but the family settles in Haran. After Terah's death, the narrative turns to God's call for Abram to leave his country and kindred. God promises to make him a great nation and a blessing to other families. Abram departs at seventy-five, travels through Canaan and builds altars at places along his route.

stories.title: Abram and Lot
stories.summary: Abram and Lot separate their households. Lot settles near Sodom, and Abram later rescues him after a battle. Their growing herds make it difficult to share the same land, and disputes arise between their herdsmen. Abram lets Lot choose first; Lot chooses the well-watered plain. Later, invading kings capture Lot and his possessions. Abram pursues them and brings the captives back. Melchizedek blesses Abram, while Abram refuses the king of Sodom's offer of goods so that the king cannot claim to have made him rich.

stories.title: Hagar and Ishmael
stories.summary: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram, and Hagar conceives. After fleeing mistreatment, Hagar encounters the angel of the Lord and returns; Ishmael is born. Unable to bear a child, Sarai arranges for her Egyptian servant Hagar to bear one. Pregnancy brings conflict between the women, and Hagar flees into the wilderness. A messenger finds her by a spring, tells her to return and promises numerous descendants. Hagar names the God who sees her. She returns to Abram's household, where Ishmael is born when Abram is eighty-six.

stories.title: Abraham and Sarah’s Covenant
stories.summary: Abram and Sarai receive the names Abraham and Sarah. God promises a son named Isaac, and visitors announce his coming birth. God establishes circumcision as the covenant's sign and promises Sarah a son despite her age. Abraham asks about Ishmael, who is also promised descendants, but the covenant is to continue through Isaac. Abraham circumcises the males of his household. Later, three visitors receive his hospitality. Sarah overhears their promise, laughs within herself and is challenged with the question of whether anything is too hard for the Lord.

stories.title: Lot Leaves Sodom
stories.summary: Visitors warn Lot to leave Sodom with his family. The chapter recounts the cities’ destruction and the origins of Moab and Ben-ammi. Lot receives two visitors, and a crowd surrounds his house. The visitors warn of coming destruction, but his sons-in-law dismiss the warning. Lot, his wife and two daughters are led out; his wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. After reaching Zoar, Lot moves to a cave. His daughters make him drunk and become pregnant by him; their sons are named Moab and Ben-ammi.

stories.title: Isaac and Ishmael
stories.summary: Sarah gives birth to Isaac. Hagar and Ishmael leave Abraham’s household, and God provides water for them in the wilderness. Abraham names and circumcises Isaac, and Sarah speaks of the laughter his birth has brought. At the child's weaning feast, conflict over Ishmael leads Sarah to demand that Hagar and her son leave. Abraham is distressed but sends them away. When their water runs out, God hears the boy and shows Hagar a well. Ishmael grows up in the wilderness and becomes an archer.

stories.title: The Binding of Isaac
stories.summary: God tells Abraham to offer Isaac. A messenger stops Abraham, and a ram is offered in Isaac’s place. Abraham travels with Isaac to the appointed mountain, carrying the materials for an offering. Isaac asks where the lamb is, and Abraham answers that God will provide. Abraham binds his son and raises the knife before the messenger calls him to stop. He sees a ram caught in a thicket and offers it instead. The promise of numerous descendants is repeated before the travelers return.

stories.title: Isaac and Rebekah
stories.summary: Abraham’s servant travels to his master’s relatives to seek a wife for Isaac. Rebekah agrees to leave with him and marries Isaac. At a well, the servant asks for a sign: a woman who offers water both to him and to his camels. Rebekah does so, and he learns that she belongs to Abraham's extended family. Her household hears his account and agrees to the marriage. Asked whether she will go, Rebekah says yes. She travels with the servant, meets Isaac and becomes his wife after the death of his mother Sarah.

stories.title: Jacob and Esau
stories.summary: Isaac and Rebekah’s sons grow up with different roles. Esau sells his birthright, Jacob receives Isaac’s blessing, and Jacob leaves for Paddan-aram. The twins struggle even before birth, and Rebekah is told that the elder will serve the younger. Esau becomes a hunter and Jacob stays near the tents. Esau exchanges his birthright for food. Later, Rebekah helps Jacob impersonate Esau before their aging father. The deception secures the blessing and provokes Esau's anger. Jacob is sent away to find a wife among Rebekah's relatives.

stories.title: Jacob’s Household
stories.summary: Jacob reaches Laban’s household and marries Leah and Rachel. Their household grows through children born to Leah, Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah. Jacob works seven years for Rachel, but Laban gives him Leah at the wedding. He then marries Rachel and agrees to further service. Rivalry shapes the household as Leah bears children and Rachel remains childless. Both women give their servants to Jacob, and children are born to Bilhah and Zilpah as well. The account names the sons and Dinah before Rachel finally gives birth to Joseph.

stories.title: Jacob Returns to Canaan
stories.summary: Jacob leaves Laban, wrestles through the night and receives the name Israel. He meets Esau and settles near Shechem. Rachel takes Laban's household images without Jacob's knowledge. Laban pursues the departing family, but the two men eventually make a boundary agreement. As Jacob approaches Esau, he sends gifts ahead and divides his company out of fear. During the night he wrestles with a mysterious opponent and receives a new name and a lasting injury. Esau embraces him at their reunion, and the brothers then go separate ways.

stories.title: Dinah at Shechem
stories.summary: Shechem violates Dinah and seeks to marry her. Her brothers Simeon and Levi attack the city, and Jacob fears retaliation. Shechem's father Hamor proposes intermarriage between the households. Dinah's brothers answer deceitfully, requiring the city's males to be circumcised. While the men recover, Simeon and Levi kill them, including Hamor and Shechem, and bring Dinah out. The other brothers plunder the city and take captives. Jacob objects that the attack has endangered his household among the surrounding peoples; his sons answer by pointing to Dinah's treatment.

stories.title: The Death of Rachel
stories.summary: Jacob returns to Bethel. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and the chapter lists Jacob’s twelve sons and recounts Isaac’s death. Jacob instructs his household to put away foreign gods before traveling to Bethel, where he builds an altar. God repeats the name Israel and the promise of descendants and land. Rachel goes into hard labor on the journey and dies after giving birth to her second son. Jacob calls him Benjamin and marks her grave. The chapter also records Reuben's act with Bilhah and the burial of Isaac by Esau and Jacob.

stories.title: Joseph and His Brothers
stories.summary: Joseph’s dreams and his father’s favour stir conflict with his brothers. They sell Joseph, and he is taken to Egypt. Jacob gives Joseph a distinctive coat, and Joseph reports dreams in which his family bows to him. Sent to find his brothers, he is stripped and thrown into a pit. The brothers then sell him to traders and stain his coat with a goat's blood. Jacob concludes that a wild animal has killed his son. Meanwhile, Joseph reaches Egypt and is sold to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh.

stories.title: Judah and Tamar
stories.summary: Tamar seeks offspring after Judah fails to give her his son Shelah. Judah acknowledges her claim, and she gives birth to Perez and Zerah. Tamar is first married to Er and then to his brother Onan; both die. Judah tells her to remain a widow while Shelah grows, but does not arrange the promised marriage. Tamar disguises herself, and Judah gives her his seal, cord and staff as a pledge. When her pregnancy is discovered, those objects identify him as the father. Judah acknowledges his failure, and the account closes with the twins' birth.

stories.title: Joseph in Egypt
stories.summary: Joseph serves in Egypt, is imprisoned, and interprets dreams. Pharaoh appoints him to store grain before a famine. Potiphar puts Joseph in charge of his household, but an accusation by Potiphar's wife sends Joseph to prison. There he interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker. The cupbearer later remembers him when Pharaoh dreams of cattle and ears of grain. Joseph explains the coming years of plenty and famine and advises storing food. Appointed over the plan, he gathers grain, marries Asenath and has two sons.

stories.title: Joseph Reunites His Family
stories.summary: Joseph’s brothers come to Egypt for food. Joseph reveals his identity, and Jacob’s household moves to Egypt. Joseph recognizes his brothers, but they do not recognize him. He tests them, holds Simeon and insists that Benjamin come on their next journey. A silver cup placed in Benjamin's sack leads Judah to offer himself in his brother's place. Joseph then makes himself known and sends for Jacob. The family settles in Goshen, and Joseph arranges provisions for them during the continuing famine.

stories.title: Jacob Blesses His Family
stories.summary: Jacob blesses Joseph’s sons and addresses his own sons before his death. The book closes with Joseph’s reconciliation with his brothers and his death in Egypt. Jacob adopts Ephraim and Manasseh into his family and places the younger before the elder in his blessing. He then speaks to each of his sons and requests burial in the family cave in Canaan. After the funeral, Joseph's brothers fear revenge, but he reassures them and promises to provide for their households. Before dying, Joseph asks that his bones be carried out when God brings the family from Egypt.

stories.title: Israel Oppressed in Egypt
stories.summary: Jacob's descendants multiply in Egypt until a new king enslaves them and orders the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn boys. The midwives refuse, and Pharaoh then commands that the boys be thrown into the Nile. The new ruler fears that the growing Israelite population could join an enemy. Forced labor on store cities and harsh service fail to stop their increase. Shiphrah and Puah, the named midwives, fear God and do not obey the order to kill boys at birth. Pharaoh then extends the command to all his people, ordering sons cast into the river while daughters are spared.

stories.title: The Birth and Rescue of Moses
stories.summary: A Levite woman hides her baby for three months, then places him in a basket among the reeds by the riverbank. Pharaoh's daughter finds him, his sister arranges for his own mother to nurse him, and he becomes the princess's son and is named Moses. His mother coats the basket with pitch, and his sister watches from a distance. When Pharaoh's daughter opens it, the crying child is recognized as a Hebrew baby. The sister offers to find a nurse and brings the child's mother, who is paid to care for him. After he grows, he is brought to Pharaoh's daughter. She names him Moses in connection with drawing him out of the water.

stories.title: Moses Flees to Midian
stories.summary: Moses kills an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, learns the deed is known, and flees to Midian. There he defends the daughters of Reuel at a well, marries Zipporah, and has a son, while God hears Israel's groaning in Egypt. The next day, Moses tries to stop two Hebrews fighting, but one challenges his authority and mentions the killing. Pharaoh hears of it and seeks Moses's life. In Midian, Moses waters the women's flock after driving off the shepherds who had pushed them aside. Reuel welcomes him, and Zipporah bears Gershom. The account ends with God remembering the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as Israel cries out.

stories.title: The Burning Bush
stories.summary: At Horeb, God speaks to Moses from a bush that burns without being consumed and sends him to bring Israel out of Egypt. Moses raises objections, is given signs, and Aaron is appointed to speak for him. Moses is tending his father-in-law's flock when he turns aside to see the bush. He is told to remove his shoes because the ground is holy. God says that Israel's suffering has been seen and gives Moses the name to tell the people. Moses questions his fitness and speech; the staff, the sign involving his hand and the promise of Aaron's help answer those objections.

stories.title: Moses Returns to Egypt
stories.summary: Moses leaves Midian with his family and the staff of God. During a dangerous encounter with the LORD on the journey, Zipporah circumcises her son. Aaron meets Moses, and the people of Israel believe the signs. After obtaining his father-in-law's permission, Moses sets out, and God tells him that those seeking his life are dead. God also warns that Pharaoh will resist and calls Israel his firstborn son. Following the encounter on the road, Aaron meets Moses at the mountain of God. Together they gather Israel's elders, relay the message and perform the signs. The people bow in worship on hearing that God has seen their affliction.

stories.title: Moses and Aaron Before Pharaoh
stories.summary: Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go and increases the labor by making them gather their own straw. The foremen blame Moses, and God renews his promise to deliver Israel and to bring them to the land sworn to the patriarchs. Moses and Aaron ask for a wilderness feast, but Pharaoh questions the Lord's authority and accuses the people of idleness. Their required brick quota stays the same even though straw is no longer supplied. Beaten Israelite officers appeal unsuccessfully to Pharaoh. Moses asks why the situation has worsened. God answers with promises of redemption and covenant, while the people find it hard to listen because of their suffering.

stories.title: The Plagues of Egypt
stories.summary: Through nine plagues, from the Nile turned to blood to darkness over the land, Moses and Aaron confront Pharaoh. Egypt's magicians match the first signs, then fail; Pharaoh's heart repeatedly hardens and he bargains over who may leave. Frogs, lice, flies, disease among livestock, boils, hail and locusts follow the first plague. Some warnings distinguish the Israelites' land or possessions from those of Egypt. Pharaoh sometimes admits fault or offers limited permission, but withdraws when relief comes. By the darkness plague, the dispute includes whether the livestock may leave. Moses insists that the animals must go too because the people do not yet know what offerings will be required.

stories.title: The Passover and the Death of the Firstborn
stories.summary: God announces the death of Egypt's firstborn and gives Israel the Passover instructions: a lamb, blood on the doorposts, and unleavened bread. At midnight the firstborn die, and Pharaoh sends Israel out as Egyptians give them silver, gold and clothing. Households are instructed to eat the meal ready to depart and to remember the event in future generations. Moses warns that a great cry will rise through Egypt, while Israel is to be protected. After the deaths, Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron during the night and tells them to go with their people and flocks. The departing Israelites carry dough before it has been leavened.

stories.title: The Exodus from Egypt
stories.summary: Israel leaves Rameses, taking the bones of Joseph, with the firstborn consecrated to the LORD. A pillar of cloud by day and fire by night guides the people. The departure includes a mixed multitude and livestock. Instructions connect unleavened bread and the dedication of firstborn offspring with remembering deliverance from slavery. The route avoids the nearer way through the land of the Philistines because the people might turn back if faced with war. Moses carries Joseph's bones in fulfillment of the earlier oath, and the guiding pillars remain before the travelers.

stories.title: Crossing the Sea
stories.summary: Pharaoh pursues Israel to the sea. The waters divide for Israel to cross on dry ground and return over the Egyptian army. Moses and Miriam lead the people in songs of praise. Trapped between the pursuing force and the water, the people fear that they will die in the wilderness. Moses tells them to stand and see deliverance. The pillar moves between the camps, a strong wind drives back the sea and Israel passes through. The returning waters cover the chariots and horsemen. The songs that follow recount the rescue and praise the Lord's power over the pursuers.

stories.title: Bitter Water, Manna and Quail
stories.summary: Israel finds bitter water at Marah, which is made sweet, and then grumbles for food in the wilderness. Quail arrive in the evening and manna in the morning, with a double portion of manna gathered before the Sabbath. The bitter water is changed after Moses casts a tree into it. At Elim, the travelers find springs and palm trees. In the wilderness, they remember the food of Egypt and complain of hunger. Manna must be gathered by household need; hoarded portions spoil, except for the portion kept for the Sabbath. A measure is preserved as a reminder of the food supplied during the wilderness years.

stories.title: Water from the Rock and the Battle with Amalek
stories.summary: At Rephidim the people quarrel over water, and Moses strikes the rock at Horeb. Amalek attacks; Israel prevails while Moses's hands are held up by Aaron and Hur. God directs Moses to take the elders and the staff with which he struck the river. Water comes from the rock, and the place is named in connection with the people's quarrel and testing. In the battle, Joshua leads the fighting while Moses stands on a hill. Aaron and Hur support his tired hands until sunset. After victory, Moses builds an altar and records the conflict with Amalek.

stories.title: Jethro Advises Moses
stories.summary: Jethro brings Moses's wife and sons to the camp, praises the LORD, and sees Moses judging the people alone. He advises appointing capable men over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens to hear lesser cases. Moses tells Jethro what happened in Egypt and on the journey. Jethro rejoices, offers sacrifices and shares a meal with Aaron and the elders. Watching the long queue of people seeking judgment, he warns that Moses and the people will wear themselves out. His plan leaves difficult cases with Moses while appointed leaders handle smaller matters. Moses follows the advice, and Jethro returns to his own land.

stories.title: The Covenant and Ten Commandments at Sinai
stories.summary: Israel camps before Mount Sinai and is told to prepare. The LORD descends in fire and speaks the Ten Commandments to the people, who fear and ask Moses to speak to them instead. Moses carries messages between the people and God, and boundaries are set around the mountain. Thunder, lightning, a thick cloud and a trumpet accompany the descent. The commandments address worship, God's name, the Sabbath, parents and conduct toward other people. Frightened by what they see and hear, the people stand at a distance. Moses approaches the thick darkness while explaining that the encounter is meant to turn them from sin.

stories.title: The Covenant Is Sealed at Sinai
stories.summary: Moses reads the book of the covenant to the people, who agree to obey, and seals the covenant with blood. Moses, Aaron and the elders ascend the mountain; Moses then enters the cloud and remains on the mountain for forty days and nights. An altar and twelve pillars represent the covenant assembly. Moses sprinkles blood and records the people's commitment to the words that have been read. Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders accompany him for part of the ascent, where they see the God of Israel and eat and drink. Moses then goes farther with Joshua, leaving Aaron and Hur available to hear disputes while he receives the stone tablets.

stories.title: The Golden Calf
stories.summary: When Moses delays, Aaron makes a golden calf and the people feast and play before it. Moses breaks the tablets, the Levites strike down about three thousand, and Moses pleads for the people. Aaron collects gold earrings, fashions the calf and announces a feast. God tells Moses what has happened and threatens to destroy the people, but Moses intercedes. Descending with the tablets, he sees the celebration, breaks the stones and destroys the calf. He confronts Aaron and calls for those on the Lord's side. After the killings, Moses returns to plead for forgiveness, and the chapter ends with a plague.

stories.title: Moses Sees God's Glory
stories.summary: The LORD says he will not go in Israel's midst, then relents. Moses asks to see his glory, is placed in a cleft of the rock, and receives a second set of tablets; his face shines afterward. The people mourn after hearing that the divine presence may not accompany them. Moses speaks with the Lord at the tent outside the camp and asks for assurance for the journey. New tablets are cut, the divine name and character are proclaimed, and covenant instructions are renewed. After forty days and nights, Moses descends with a radiant face, covering his face with a veil between encounters with the Lord and the people.

stories.title: Building the Tabernacle
stories.summary: The people bring more than enough materials, and Bezaleel and Aholiab oversee the work. The tabernacle is set up on the first day of the first month in the second year, and the cloud and glory of the LORD fill it. The account begins with the Sabbath command and an invitation for willing gifts. Skilled workers make the curtains, frames, ark, table, lampstand, altars, courtyard and priestly garments according to the instructions. Moses inspects and blesses the completed work. After the furnishings are arranged and the priests prepared, the glory fills the sanctuary. The cloud's resting or lifting determines when the people camp or continue their journey.

stories.title: Aaron and His Sons Are Ordained
stories.summary: Moses washes, clothes and anoints Aaron and his sons over seven days. On the eighth day they offer the first sacrifices and fire from the LORD consumes the offering on the altar.

stories.title: Nadab and Abihu
stories.summary: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire and are consumed by fire from the LORD. Moses forbids mourning by Aaron and his remaining sons and gives instructions about wine and the priests' portions.

stories.title: The Blasphemer Stoned
stories.summary: The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man curses the Name in a fight. After the LORD is consulted, the congregation stones him, and the principle of equal justice for native and sojourner is restated.

stories.title: Counting the Camp
stories.summary: At Sinai the LORD commands Moses and Aaron to count the men of Israel aged twenty and over who can go to war. They assemble the congregation and take the census by tribe; the Levites are excluded from this count.

stories.title: Offerings and the Passover at Sinai
stories.summary: The tribal leaders present offerings for the altar, the Levites are set apart, and Israel keeps the Passover, with a later date allowed for those unclean. The cloud over the tabernacle signals when to move or camp.

stories.title: Leaving Sinai and the Complaints
stories.summary: Israel leaves Sinai in marching order. The people complain about manna and crave meat, Moses shares his burden with seventy elders, and the LORD sends quail followed by a plague.

stories.title: Miriam and Aaron Speak Against Moses
stories.summary: Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses over his Ethiopian wife and claim to speak for God. The LORD defends Moses, strikes Miriam with leprosy, and she is shut out of the camp for seven days.

stories.title: The Twelve Spies
stories.summary: Twelve men scout Canaan. Ten report the people are too strong; Joshua and Caleb urge Israel to enter. The people rebel, and God decrees that the generation will die in the wilderness over forty years.

stories.title: Korah's Rebellion
stories.summary: Korah, Dathan and Abiram challenge Moses and Aaron. The ground swallows the rebels and fire consumes the 250 incense-bearers; afterward Aaron's rod buds to confirm the priesthood.

stories.title: Water from the Rock at Meribah
stories.summary: After Miriam dies, the people again lack water. Moses strikes the rock twice instead of speaking to it, and the LORD tells Moses and Aaron they will not lead the people into the land.

stories.title: Edom Refuses Passage and Aaron Dies
stories.summary: Edom refuses to let Israel pass through its land. At Mount Hor Aaron's garments are placed on Eleazar and Aaron dies.

stories.title: The Bronze Serpent
stories.summary: The people speak against God and Moses, and fiery serpents bite them. Moses makes a bronze serpent on a pole, and those who look at it live.

stories.title: Victories over Sihon and Og
stories.summary: Israel travels around Moab, sings at the well, and defeats Sihon of the Amorites and Og of Bashan, taking their lands east of the Jordan.

stories.title: Balaam and Balak
stories.summary: Balak of Moab hires Balaam to curse Israel. Balaam's donkey sees the angel of the LORD, and Balaam blesses Israel instead, ending with oracles about a star out of Jacob.

stories.title: Baal of Peor
stories.summary: Israel joins in the worship of Baal of Peor with Moabite women, and a plague strikes. Phinehas kills a man and a Midianite woman, ending the plague, and he receives a covenant of peace.

stories.title: A New Census and Joshua Appointed
stories.summary: A second census counts the new generation. The daughters of Zelophehad win the right to inherit, and Moses commissions Joshua as his successor.

stories.title: Vengeance on Midian
stories.summary: Israel makes war on Midian and kills its kings and Balaam. Moses is angry that women were spared, the plunder is divided, and the officers bring an offering for their lives.

stories.title: Tribes Settle East of the Jordan
stories.summary: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh ask for the land east of the Jordan. Moses agrees on condition that their men fight with the other tribes until the conquest is complete.

stories.title: Moses Recalls the Wilderness Years
stories.summary: On the plains of Moab Moses recounts the departure from Horeb, the spies, the forty years, and the conquests of Sihon and Og. He pleads to enter the land and is told to commission Joshua instead.

stories.title: Moses Sets Apart Three Cities of Refuge
stories.summary: Moses sets apart Bezer, Ramoth and Golan east of the Jordan as cities where someone who kills a neighbor unintentionally, without prior hatred, may flee and live.

stories.title: Moses Recalls the Golden Calf
stories.summary: Moses recalls receiving the stone tablets at Horeb, finding Israel worshiping a molten calf, and breaking the tablets. He recounts destroying the calf and interceding for Israel and Aaron after the LORD threatened destruction.

stories.title: Moses Recalls the Second Tablets
stories.summary: Moses recalls making an ark and two stone tablets, going up the mountain, and placing the tablets written by the LORD inside the ark. He also recalls his intercession and the command to lead the people onward.

stories.title: Joshua Commissioned and the Law Entrusted
stories.summary: Moses tells Israel that Joshua will lead them across the Jordan and encourages Joshua before the people. He delivers the written law to the priests, appears with Joshua at the tabernacle, and writes and teaches a song as a witness for Israel.

stories.title: The Death of Moses
stories.summary: Moses climbs Mount Nebo, sees the promised land, and dies at 120 in Moab. Israel mourns thirty days, and Joshua, filled with the spirit of wisdom, succeeds him.

stories.title: Joshua Commissioned
stories.summary: After Moses dies, the LORD charges Joshua to be strong, keep the law and lead Israel across the Jordan. The eastern tribes pledge to follow him.

stories.title: Rahab and the Spies
stories.summary: Two spies sent to Jericho are hidden by Rahab, who says the city's people fear Israel's God. She asks for protection for her family and is told to mark her window with a scarlet cord.

stories.title: Crossing the Jordan
stories.summary: As the priests carrying the ark step into the Jordan, the waters stop flowing and Israel crosses on dry ground. Twelve stones are set up as a memorial at Gilgal.

stories.title: Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal
stories.summary: Israel circumcises the men born in the wilderness, keeps the Passover, and the manna ceases. A commander of the LORD's army appears to Joshua near Jericho.

stories.title: The Fall of Jericho
stories.summary: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days, and on the seventh day the walls fall at the shout. The city is devoted to destruction; Rahab and her family are spared.

stories.title: Achan's Sin and Ai
stories.summary: Achan takes devoted goods from Jericho, and Israel is defeated at Ai. After Achan is identified and stoned, Israel takes Ai by ambush and renews the covenant at Ebal and Gerizim.

stories.title: The Gibeonite Deception
stories.summary: The Gibeonites pose as distant travelers and trick Israel into a treaty. When the deceit is discovered, they are made woodcutters and water carriers for the altar.

stories.title: The Sun Stands Still
stories.summary: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon. Israel defeats them at Beth-horon with hailstones, and Joshua asks that the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won.

stories.title: Northern Campaign and the Land Taken
stories.summary: Joshua defeats a northern coalition under Jabin of Hazor, and the chapter lists the kings defeated on both sides of the Jordan.

stories.title: Caleb Receives Hebron
stories.summary: Caleb reminds Joshua of his faithful report as a spy and the promise Moses made to him. At eighty-five he asks for the hill country where the Anakims live, and Joshua blesses him and gives him Hebron as his inheritance.

stories.title: The Altar by the Jordan
stories.summary: The eastern tribes build a large altar by the Jordan, and the western tribes prepare for war. A delegation led by Phinehas hears that it is a witness, not a place for sacrifice, and the matter is settled.

stories.title: Joshua's Farewell and Covenant at Shechem
stories.summary: Joshua warns Israel to remain faithful, recounts God's acts since Abraham, and calls the people to choose whom they will serve. The people renew the covenant, and Joshua, Joseph's bones and Eleazar are buried.

stories.title: Incomplete Conquest
stories.summary: Judah and the other tribes take parts of the land but fail to drive out many Canaanite peoples. The angel of the LORD rebukes Israel at Bochim.

stories.title: The Cycle of the Judges
stories.summary: After Joshua's generation dies, Israel follows other gods, is oppressed, and is delivered by judges the LORD raises up. The pattern then repeats.

stories.title: Othniel, Ehud and Shamgar
stories.summary: Othniel defeats Cushan-rishathaim, and Ehud kills the Moabite king Eglon with a concealed blade and rallies Israel. Shamgar strikes down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.

stories.title: Deborah and Barak
stories.summary: Deborah summons Barak to fight Sisera's chariots. Sisera is killed by Jael with a tent peg, and Deborah and Barak sing a victory song.

stories.title: Gideon and the Midianites
stories.summary: The angel of the LORD calls Gideon, who tears down his father's Baal altar and tests God with a fleece. Reduced to three hundred men, he routs Midian with trumpets and torches and refuses to rule.

stories.title: Abimelech
stories.summary: Gideon's son Abimelech kills his brothers and is made king at Shechem. After Jotham's fable, Shechem turns on him, and Abimelech dies when a woman drops a millstone on his head.

stories.title: Jephthah's Vow
stories.summary: Jephthah leads Gilead against Ammon and vows to offer whatever first comes out of his house, which is his daughter. He later fights Ephraim at the fords of the Jordan.

stories.title: Samson
stories.summary: Born to a barren woman and set apart as a Nazirite, Samson fights the Philistines. Betrayed by Delilah, he loses his hair, is blinded, and brings down a temple on himself and many Philistines.

stories.title: Micah's Idols and the Danites
stories.summary: Micah of Ephraim sets up a household shrine with a hired Levite. The tribe of Dan takes the idols and priest and seizes the peaceful town of Laish.

stories.title: The Levite and Gibeah
stories.summary: A Levite's concubine is abused to death at Gibeah of Benjamin. Israel goes to war against Benjamin, nearly wipes it out, and then arranges wives for the survivors.

stories.title: Naomi and Ruth Return to Bethlehem
stories.summary: A famine drives Elimelech's family to Moab, where he and his sons die. Naomi returns to Bethlehem, and her daughter-in-law Ruth refuses to leave her.

stories.title: Ruth Gleans in Boaz's Field
stories.summary: Ruth gleans barley in the field of Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband. Boaz shows her kindness and extra grain.

stories.title: The Threshing Floor
stories.summary: On Naomi's advice Ruth lies at Boaz's feet at the threshing floor. Boaz promises to act as redeemer if a nearer kinsman declines.

stories.title: Boaz Redeems and Marries Ruth
stories.summary: At the city gate the nearer kinsman gives up his right, and Boaz buys Elimelech's land and marries Ruth. Their son Obed becomes the grandfather of David.

stories.title: Hannah and the Birth of Samuel
stories.summary: Barren Hannah prays at Shiloh and vows to dedicate a son to the LORD. She bears Samuel, brings him to Eli, and sings a song of thanksgiving.

stories.title: Eli's Sons and Samuel's Call
stories.summary: Eli's sons abuse their priestly office, and a man of God announces judgment on Eli's house. The LORD calls the boy Samuel by night and confirms him as a prophet.

stories.title: The Ark Captured and Returned
stories.summary: Israel loses the ark to the Philistines, and Eli and his sons die. The ark brings plagues on Philistine cities and is sent back on a cart to Beth-shemesh. The men of Kirjath-jearim then take it to Abinadab’s house.

stories.title: Samuel Judges Israel
stories.summary: Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods, and the LORD thunders against the Philistines at Mizpah. The stone Ebenezer marks the victory.

stories.title: Israel Demands a King
stories.summary: The elders ask Samuel for a king. Saul of Benjamin is anointed, chosen by lot, and confirmed after defeating the Ammonites at Jabesh-gilead; Samuel gives a farewell address.

stories.title: Saul Rejected
stories.summary: Saul offers sacrifice before Samuel arrives and later spares King Agag and the best of the Amalekite livestock. Samuel tells him the kingdom will be taken from him.

stories.title: David Anointed
stories.summary: Samuel anoints David, the youngest son of Jesse, at Bethlehem. David joins Saul's court to play the lyre when an evil spirit troubles the king.

stories.title: David and Goliath
stories.summary: The Philistine champion Goliath challenges Israel for forty days. David, armed with a sling and five stones, kills him in the name of the LORD.

stories.title: Saul's Jealousy and David's Flight
stories.summary: Jonathan makes a covenant with David, Saul grows jealous of his success and tries to kill him, and David escapes with help from Michal, Jonathan and the priest Ahimelech.

stories.title: David in the Wilderness
stories.summary: David gathers followers at Adullam, Saul has the priests of Nob killed, and David spares Saul's life in a cave at En-gedi and in the camp at Ziph. Abigail intervenes to keep David from killing her husband Nabal.

stories.title: Saul and the Medium at Endor; Saul's Death
stories.summary: Saul consults a medium at Endor and is told he will die. David is dismissed from the Philistine army and defeats the Amalekites at Ziklag; Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa.

stories.title: David Becomes King
stories.summary: David mourns Saul and Jonathan and is anointed king of Judah at Hebron. After Abner and Ish-bosheth are killed, the tribes of Israel anoint him as well.

stories.title: Jerusalem and the Ark
stories.summary: David takes Jerusalem and defeats the Philistines. Uzzah dies touching the ark during an attempted transfer; David later brings it to the city with rejoicing, and Michal scorns his dancing.

stories.title: The Davidic Covenant
stories.summary: David wishes to build a house for the LORD, but through Nathan God promises to build David a house and establish his throne forever.

stories.title: David and Mephibosheth
stories.summary: David wins wars on all sides, shows kindness to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, and defeats the Ammonites and Arameans.

stories.title: David, Bathsheba and Uriah
stories.summary: David takes Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, and has Uriah killed in battle. Nathan confronts him with a parable, and David confesses; their first child dies and Solomon is born.

stories.title: Amnon, Tamar and Absalom
stories.summary: Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar, and Absalom has Amnon killed and flees. Joab arranges Absalom's return to Jerusalem.

stories.title: Absalom's Rebellion
stories.summary: Absalom wins the people's loyalty and David flees Jerusalem. Absalom is killed in the forest of Ephraim, and David returns across the Jordan.

stories.title: Sheba's Revolt and the Gibeonites
stories.summary: Sheba leads a northern revolt that Joab ends at Abel. A famine is traced to Saul's treatment of the Gibeonites, and seven of Saul's descendants are handed over.

stories.title: The Exploits of David's Mighty Men
stories.summary: The account recalls the deeds of David's mighty men, including three warriors who bring him water from Bethlehem and Benaiah's victories. David refuses to drink the water obtained at such risk and pours it out to the LORD.

stories.title: The Census and the Plague
stories.summary: David orders a census of Israel and Judah and then repents. A plague falls on Israel, and David buys Araunah's threshing floor to build an altar.

stories.title: Solomon Becomes King
stories.summary: Adonijah tries to take the throne as David grows old, but Nathan and Bathsheba secure Solomon's anointing. David charges Solomon and dies, and Solomon removes his rivals.

stories.title: Solomon's Wisdom
stories.summary: At Gibeon Solomon asks God for an understanding heart. He judges between two women claiming one child, and his wisdom is praised.

stories.title: The Temple Built
stories.summary: Solomon builds the temple with materials from Hiram of Tyre, installs the ark, and prays at its dedication as the glory of the LORD fills the house.

stories.title: The Queen of Sheba and Solomon's Decline
stories.summary: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon and is amazed. Solomon takes many foreign wives who turn his heart to other gods, and God raises adversaries against him.

stories.title: The Kingdom Divides
stories.summary: Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice, and the northern tribes follow Jeroboam. Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

stories.title: The Man of God from Judah
stories.summary: A man of God from Judah prophesies against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, then disobeys and is killed by a lion. Ahijah announces the end of Jeroboam's house.

stories.title: Zimri's Coup and Omri's Rise
stories.summary: Zimri murders Elah and destroys Baasha’s household. The army makes Omri king and besieges Tirzah; Zimri burns the royal house over himself and dies. After a struggle with Tibni’s supporters, Omri reigns and builds Samaria.

stories.title: Elijah and the Drought
stories.summary: Elijah announces a drought, is fed by ravens, and stays with a widow at Zarephath whose flour and oil do not run out. He raises her son.

stories.title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
stories.summary: Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal to a contest of sacrifice on Carmel. Fire falls on his altar, the prophets are killed, and rain returns.

stories.title: Elijah at Horeb
stories.summary: Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees to Horeb and hears the LORD in a gentle whisper. He is told to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, and he calls Elisha.

stories.title: Naboth's Vineyard
stories.summary: Ahab wants Naboth's vineyard, and Jezebel arranges for Naboth to be falsely accused and stoned. Elijah announces judgment on Ahab's house.

stories.title: Ahab and Micaiah
stories.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat ask prophets about attacking Ramoth-gilead. Micaiah alone predicts defeat, and Ahab is killed in the battle.

stories.title: Elijah Taken Up
stories.summary: Elijah calls down fire on soldiers sent by King Ahaziah, then is taken up in a whirlwind as Elisha watches. Elisha takes his mantle and heals the waters of Jericho.

stories.title: Elisha and Moab
stories.summary: Israel, Judah and Edom march against Moab and run out of water. Elisha predicts water and victory, and the Moabite king offers his son on the wall.

stories.title: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son
stories.summary: Elisha multiplies a widow's oil, promises a son to the Shunammite woman and later raises him, purifies a poisoned stew, and feeds a hundred men with twenty loaves.

stories.title: Naaman Healed
stories.summary: Naaman, an Aramean commander with a skin disease, is healed by washing seven times in the Jordan. Elisha's servant Gehazi takes a reward and is struck with the disease.

stories.title: Elisha and the Arameans
stories.summary: Elisha recovers a lost axe head, leads blinded Aramean soldiers to Samaria, and predicts the end of a siege. Four lepers discover the Aramean camp abandoned.

stories.title: Jehu's Revolt
stories.summary: Elisha's messenger anoints Jehu, who kills Joram and Ahaziah, has Jezebel thrown from a window, wipes out Ahab's house and Baal's worshipers, and keeps the golden calves.

stories.title: Athaliah and Joash
stories.summary: Athaliah destroys the royal family except the infant Joash, who is hidden in the temple. After six years the priest Jehoiada crowns him, and Joash repairs the temple.

stories.title: Elisha's Death and Israel's Victories
stories.summary: Elisha dies after prophesying Israel's victories over Syria, and a dead man is revived when he touches Elisha's bones. Jehoash of Israel defeats Amaziah of Judah, and Jeroboam II restores Israel's borders.

stories.title: The Fall of Samaria
stories.summary: Kings follow one another in Israel and Judah until Assyria conquers Samaria and deports its people. Foreign settlers bring their own gods into the land.

stories.title: Hezekiah and Sennacherib
stories.summary: Hezekiah removes the high places and is besieged by Sennacherib of Assyria. Isaiah promises deliverance, and the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp.

stories.title: Hezekiah's Illness and the Babylonian Envoys
stories.summary: Hezekiah is healed and given fifteen more years, with the shadow going back ten steps. He shows Babylonian envoys his treasures, and Isaiah foretells exile.

stories.title: Manasseh, Amon and Josiah
stories.summary: Manasseh and Amon turn Judah to idolatry. During Josiah’s reign Hilkiah finds the book of the law in the temple; Josiah renews the covenant, removes idols and keeps a great Passover before dying at Megiddo.

stories.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
stories.summary: Babylon besieges Jerusalem, destroys the temple, and takes Judah into exile under Nebuchadnezzar. Gedaliah is killed, and Jehoiachin is freed in Babylon.

stories.title: The Death of Saul
stories.summary: Saul and his sons die on Mount Gilboa, and the chronicler says Saul died for his unfaithfulness, including consulting a medium.

stories.title: David Takes Jerusalem and Gathers His Warriors
stories.summary: All Israel anoints David at Hebron. He captures Jerusalem, and the lists name his mighty men and the troops who joined him.

stories.title: The Ark Brought to Jerusalem
stories.summary: Uzzah dies when the ark is moved on a cart, and David leaves it with Obed-edom. He then brings it to Jerusalem with the Levites carrying it and appoints singers.

stories.title: God's Covenant with David and His Wars
stories.summary: Through Nathan God promises David a lasting dynasty. David wins wars against the Philistines, Moab, Aram and Ammon.

stories.title: The Census and the Temple Site
stories.summary: Satan incites David to number Israel, and a plague follows. David buys Ornan's threshing floor and starts gathering materials for the temple, which Solomon will build.

stories.title: David's Last Charge and Death
stories.summary: David presents the temple plans to Solomon, the leaders give freely, and David prays. Solomon is crowned a second time, and David dies after a reign of forty years.

stories.title: Solomon Builds the Temple
stories.summary: Solomon asks for wisdom at Gibeon, builds the temple with Huram of Tyre's help, brings in the ark, and prays at the dedication as fire and glory fill the house.

stories.title: Solomon's Reign and the Queen of Sheba
stories.summary: Solomon builds cities, arranges temple worship, and receives the queen of Sheba and tribute before his death.

stories.title: Rehoboam and the Division
stories.summary: Rehoboam's harsh answer splits the kingdom. Shishak of Egypt attacks Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year, and the king humbles himself.

stories.title: Abijah and Asa
stories.summary: Abijah defeats Jeroboam, and Asa removes idols and defeats Zerah the Cushite. Late in life Asa relies on Aram and consults physicians rather than the LORD.

stories.title: Jehoshaphat
stories.summary: Jehoshaphat sends officials to teach the law and allies with Ahab. He later faces a coalition of Moab and Ammon, and Judah sings as the enemies destroy one another.

stories.title: Jehoram, Ahaziah, Athaliah and Joash
stories.summary: Jehoram kills his brothers, and Athaliah seizes the throne until the priest Jehoiada crowns Joash. After Jehoiada's death Joash turns away and has Zechariah stoned.

stories.title: Amaziah, Uzziah and Jotham
stories.summary: Amaziah defeats Edom but worships its gods. Uzziah prospers, then enters the temple to burn incense and is struck with a skin disease; Jotham rules faithfully.

stories.title: Ahaz and Hezekiah's Reforms
stories.summary: Ahaz sacrifices to foreign gods and closes the temple. Hezekiah reopens it, cleanses it, restores worship and calls all Israel to keep the Passover.

stories.title: Sennacherib's Invasion and Hezekiah's Pride
stories.summary: Hezekiah prepares Jerusalem's defenses and water supply, and Sennacherib's army is struck down. Hezekiah's later pride is humbled.

stories.title: Manasseh's Repentance and Josiah's Reforms
stories.summary: Manasseh is taken captive to Babylon, humbles himself, and returns to remove idols. During Josiah’s reign Hilkiah finds the law book; Josiah renews the covenant, keeps a great Passover, and dies fighting Pharaoh Necho.

stories.title: The Fall of Judah and Cyrus's Decree
stories.summary: Judah's last kings fall to Nebuchadnezzar, the temple is burned, and the land lies desolate seventy years. Cyrus of Persia then decrees that the temple be rebuilt.

stories.title: Cyrus's Decree and the Return
stories.summary: Cyrus of Persia authorizes the Jews to return and rebuild the temple and returns the temple vessels. A list records those who go back under Zerubbabel and Jeshua.

stories.title: Rebuilding the Altar and Foundation
stories.summary: The returnees rebuild the altar, keep the Feast of Booths, and lay the temple foundation to shouts of joy and weeping from the older generation.

stories.title: Opposition and Delay
stories.summary: Opponents offer to help rebuild the temple, are refused, and obstruct the work. The chapter also recounts later letters that lead Artaxerxes to stop work on Jerusalem’s city; it closes by returning to the temple work halted until Darius’s reign.

stories.title: The Temple Completed
stories.summary: Haggai and Zechariah urge the people to resume building. Darius finds Cyrus's decree and orders the work supported, and the temple is dedicated and Passover kept.

stories.title: Ezra Comes to Jerusalem
stories.summary: Ezra, a priest and scribe, receives a royal commission from Artaxerxes and leads a group of exiles to Jerusalem after fasting for safe passage.

stories.title: Ezra and Mixed Marriages
stories.summary: Ezra learns that many Israelites have married foreign wives. He prays in distress, and the assembly agrees to send away the foreign wives.

stories.title: Nehemiah's Prayer and Commission
stories.summary: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, hears that Jerusalem's walls are broken. He prays, then asks the king for leave and letters of passage to rebuild.

stories.title: Rebuilding the Wall
stories.summary: Nehemiah inspects the ruined wall by night and organizes the people to rebuild. Sanballat and Tobiah mock and plot, so Nehemiah assigns guards while the builders work armed.

stories.title: Debt Relief
stories.summary: Poor families are losing land and children to debt. Nehemiah rebukes the nobles, they return what they took, and he refuses the governor's food allowance.

stories.title: The Wall Completed
stories.summary: Plots against Nehemiah fail, and the wall is finished in fifty-two days. A register of those who returned is recovered.

stories.title: Ezra Reads the Law
stories.summary: Ezra reads the law to the assembly, the Levites explain it, and the people keep the Feast of Booths. They confess their sins and recount Israel's history in prayer.

stories.title: The Dedication of Jerusalem’s Wall
stories.summary: The Levites and singers gather for the dedication of Jerusalem’s wall. Two companies give thanks as they proceed along the wall and meet at the house of God; sacrifices and rejoicing follow.

stories.title: Nehemiah's Reforms
stories.summary: On a return from Persia, Nehemiah removes Tobiah from a temple room, restores tithes, shuts the gates on the Sabbath, and confronts those who married foreign women.

stories.title: Vashti Deposed
stories.summary: King Ahasuerus holds a long feast, and Queen Vashti refuses his summons. He deposes her on the advice of his counselors.

stories.title: Esther Becomes Queen
stories.summary: Esther, a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, is chosen as queen without revealing her people. Mordecai exposes a plot against the king.

stories.title: Haman's Plot
stories.summary: Haman is angered that Mordecai will not bow and persuades the king to decree the destruction of the Jews. Mordecai urges Esther to intervene, and she asks the Jews to fast.

stories.title: Esther's Banquets
stories.summary: Esther invites the king and Haman to two banquets. The king, reminded of Mordecai's service, honors him, and Esther exposes Haman, who is hanged on the gallows he built.

stories.title: The Jews Delivered and Purim
stories.summary: A new decree lets the Jews defend themselves, and they overcome their enemies. The days of Purim are established, and Mordecai rises to high office.

stories.title: Job's Testing
stories.summary: Job is a blameless man whose wealth and children are taken after Satan challenges his motives before God. When his health is struck as well, his wife urges him to curse God, and three friends come to sit with him.

stories.title: Elihu Speaks
stories.summary: A younger man, Elihu, speaks after Job's three friends fall silent. He says he is angry with Job for justifying himself and with the friends for failing to answer him.

stories.title: God Answers from the Whirlwind
stories.summary: The LORD answers Job out of the whirlwind with questions about creation, the animals, Behemoth and Leviathan.

stories.title: Job Restored
stories.summary: Job answers that he has spoken of things too wonderful for him. God rebukes the three friends, Job prays for them, and his wealth is doubled and new children are born.

stories.title: Isaiah's Call
stories.summary: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the LORD on a throne and a seraph touches his lips with a coal. He is sent to a people who will not understand.

stories.title: Ahaz and the Sign of Immanuel
stories.summary: Syria and Israel threaten Judah. Isaiah tells King Ahaz to stand firm, and when Ahaz refuses to ask for a sign, Isaiah announces that a virgin shall conceive and bear a son called Immanuel.

stories.title: Sennacherib's Threat and Hezekiah
stories.summary: The Assyrian field commander demands Jerusalem's surrender. Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's letter before the LORD, Isaiah promises deliverance, and the Assyrian camp is struck down.

stories.title: Hezekiah's Illness
stories.summary: Hezekiah is told to prepare to die, prays, and is given fifteen more years. He shows Babylonian envoys his treasures, and Isaiah foretells that they will be carried to Babylon.

stories.title: Jeremiah's Call
stories.summary: The LORD calls Jeremiah as a young man to be a prophet to the nations. He is shown an almond branch and a boiling pot and told not to fear.

stories.title: The Potter's House and the Broken Jar
stories.summary: Jeremiah watches a potter remake a spoiled vessel, then breaks a clay jar in the Valley of Hinnom to announce coming destruction.

stories.title: Jeremiah and Pashhur
stories.summary: The priest Pashhur has Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks. After his release Jeremiah announces judgment on Pashhur and complains bitterly about his calling.

stories.title: Hananiah's False Prophecy
stories.summary: Hananiah breaks the yoke Jeremiah wears and says Babylon's rule will end in two years. Jeremiah answers that the yoke will be iron, and Hananiah dies that year.

stories.title: The Scroll Burned
stories.summary: Baruch writes down Jeremiah's words and reads them in the temple. King Jehoiakim cuts the scroll and burns it, and Jeremiah dictates it again with additions.

stories.title: Jeremiah in the Cistern
stories.summary: During the siege Jeremiah is arrested and lowered into a muddy cistern. Ebed-melech the Cushite pulls him out, and Zedekiah consults him privately.

stories.title: The Fall of Jerusalem and Flight to Egypt
stories.summary: Babylon captures Jerusalem and Jeremiah is freed. After Gedaliah is killed, the survivors ignore Jeremiah's warning and flee to Egypt, taking him with them.

stories.title: Ezekiel's Vision and Commission
stories.summary: By the Chebar canal Ezekiel sees four living creatures and wheels, is given a scroll to eat, and is made a watchman for Israel.

stories.title: The Glory Leaves the Temple
stories.summary: In a vision Ezekiel is shown idolatry in the temple. The glory of the LORD departs the city, and God promises to gather the exiles and give them a new heart.

stories.title: The Death of Ezekiel's Wife
stories.summary: The LORD tells Ezekiel that the desire of his eyes will be taken away and commands him not to perform the usual mourning rites. His wife dies that evening; he explains his conduct to the people as a sign concerning the sanctuary and their families.

stories.title: The Valley of Dry Bones
stories.summary: Ezekiel sees a valley of dry bones come to life at God's word and is told it pictures Israel's restoration. He joins two sticks as a sign that Judah and Israel will be one kingdom.

stories.title: Ezekiel Is Shown the Temple in a Vision
stories.summary: In a vision Ezekiel is brought to the land of Israel and set on a high mountain. He sees a man with a measuring reed at a gate and is told to observe what he is shown and declare it to the house of Israel.

stories.title: Daniel and His Friends in Babylon
stories.summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah to Babylon for training. They refuse the king's food, thrive on vegetables and water, and enter his service.

stories.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Statue
stories.summary: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men tell him both his dream and its interpretation. God reveals it to Daniel: a statue of gold, silver, brass, iron and clay is struck by a stone, which Daniel interprets as God’s kingdom overcoming the kingdoms represented by the statue.

stories.title: The Fiery Furnace
stories.summary: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and are thrown into a furnace. A fourth figure walks with them, and they come out unharmed.

stories.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Humbling
stories.summary: Daniel interprets a dream of a great tree cut down. The king loses his sanity for seven periods, then recovers and praises God.

stories.title: Belshazzar's Feast
stories.summary: A hand writes on the wall during Belshazzar’s feast, and Daniel reads it as a sentence on the kingdom. Belshazzar is killed that night, and Darius the Median receives the kingdom.

stories.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
stories.summary: Jealous officials trick Darius into a decree against prayer to anyone but him. Daniel keeps praying, is thrown to lions, and is found unharmed.

stories.title: Daniel's Visions
stories.summary: Daniel sees four beasts and a son of man, a ram and a goat, and receives the prayer-answer about seventy weeks and a final vision of kings and the end.

stories.title: Hosea's Marriage to Gomer
stories.summary: At the LORD’s command Hosea marries Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim. The births and symbolic names of Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah and Lo-ammi accompany messages about Israel and Judah.

stories.title: Amaziah Opposes Amos
stories.summary: The priest Amaziah tells Amos to leave Bethel and prophesy in Judah. Amos answers that he was a herdsman called by the LORD and announces judgment on Amaziah.

stories.title: Jonah Flees and Is Swallowed
stories.summary: Jonah boards a ship to Tarshish instead of going to Nineveh. A storm leads the sailors to throw him overboard, and a great fish swallows him; he prays and is cast onto land.

stories.title: Nineveh Repents
stories.summary: Jonah preaches in Nineveh, and the king and people repent in sackcloth. God relents from the disaster.

stories.title: Jonah's Anger
stories.summary: Jonah is angry that God spared Nineveh. A plant shades him and then withers; the LORD contrasts Jonah’s pity for the plant with his own pity for the great city.

stories.title: The Birth of Jesus and the Magi
stories.summary: Joseph learns in a dream that Mary's child is from the Holy Spirit. Magi follow a star to Bethlehem and bring gifts to the child.

stories.title: Flight to Egypt and Return to Nazareth
stories.summary: Warned in a dream, Joseph takes the family to Egypt while Herod kills Bethlehem's boys. After Herod dies they return and settle in Nazareth.

stories.title: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
stories.summary: John baptizes Jesus in the Jordan, and a voice from heaven speaks. Jesus fasts forty days in the wilderness and answers the devil's three temptations with scripture.

stories.title: Calling the First Disciples
stories.summary: Jesus begins preaching in Galilee and calls Simon, Andrew, James and John to follow him. Crowds come for healing.

stories.title: Healings and Calming the Storm
stories.summary: Jesus heals a leper, a centurion's servant, Peter's mother-in-law and a paralytic, calms a storm, and sends demons into pigs. He calls Matthew and raises a girl and heals a woman who touched his cloak.

stories.title: Sending Out the Twelve
stories.summary: Jesus calls his twelve disciples, gives them authority over unclean spirits and disease, and sends them out. The account names the twelve, including Judas Iscariot, who later betrays him.

stories.title: Jesus and John the Baptist
stories.summary: John, in prison, sends disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come. Jesus answers with his works and invites the weary to come to him.

stories.title: Sabbath Controversies and the Sign of Jonah
stories.summary: Jesus defends his disciples plucking grain on the Sabbath and heals a man's hand. When asked for a sign, he points to the sign of Jonah.

stories.title: Feeding the Five Thousand and Walking on Water
stories.summary: John the Baptist is beheaded by Herod. Jesus feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish and walks on the sea, and Peter briefly walks toward him.

stories.title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration
stories.summary: Peter says Jesus is the Christ, and Jesus foretells his death and resurrection. Six days later he is transfigured before Peter, James and John.

stories.title: The Rich Young Man
stories.summary: A rich young man cannot give up his possessions to follow Jesus. Jesus tells the parable of the workers in the vineyard and heals two blind men near Jericho.

stories.title: The Triumphal Entry and Temple Cleansing
stories.summary: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey, drives the merchants from the temple, curses a fig tree, and answers challenges to his authority.

stories.title: The Last Supper and Gethsemane
stories.summary: A woman anoints Jesus, Judas agrees to betray him, and Jesus shares a Passover meal with the twelve. In Gethsemane he prays, and Judas arrives with an armed crowd.

stories.title: Trial, Crucifixion and Burial
stories.summary: Jesus is tried before Caiaphas and Pilate, Peter denies him, and Judas dies. Jesus is crucified, dies, and is buried in Joseph of Arimathea's tomb.

stories.title: The Resurrection and the Great Commission
stories.summary: Women find the tomb empty and meet the risen Jesus. The guards are paid to spread a false account, and Jesus sends the eleven to make disciples of all nations.

stories.title: John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus
stories.summary: John preaches repentance in the wilderness and baptizes Jesus. The Spirit descends and Jesus is tested in the wilderness for forty days.

stories.title: Calling the Disciples and Healing in Capernaum
stories.summary: Jesus calls four fishermen, casts out an unclean spirit in the synagogue, heals Peter's mother-in-law and cleanses a leper.

stories.title: The Paralytic and Controversies
stories.summary: Four friends lower a paralytic through a roof, and Jesus forgives and heals him. Jesus calls Levi, defends his disciples on the Sabbath, and heals a withered hand.

stories.title: Parables and Calming the Storm
stories.summary: Jesus teaches by the sea in parables of the sower and the mustard seed, then calms a storm on the lake.

stories.title: The Gadarene Demoniac, Jairus and the Woman
stories.summary: Jesus sends a legion of demons into pigs, heals a woman who touched his cloak, and raises Jairus's daughter.

stories.title: Feeding the Multitude
stories.summary: Jesus feeds five thousand and walks on the lake to his disciples.

stories.title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration in Mark
stories.summary: Peter calls Jesus the Christ, and Jesus foretells his suffering. He is transfigured on a mountain and then heals a boy with an unclean spirit.

stories.title: Blind Bartimaeus
stories.summary: A blind beggar near Jericho calls out to the son of David and receives his sight.

stories.title: Triumphal Entry and the Temple
stories.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a colt, curses a fig tree, drives out the temple traders, and is challenged on his authority.

stories.title: The Last Supper and Gethsemane in Mark
stories.summary: A woman anoints Jesus at Bethany, Judas arranges the betrayal, and Jesus shares the last supper. In Gethsemane he prays and is arrested.

stories.title: Trial, Crucifixion and Burial in Mark
stories.summary: Jesus is tried by the council and Pilate, Peter denies him, and he is crucified between two criminals and buried by Joseph of Arimathea.

stories.title: The Empty Tomb
stories.summary: Women come to the tomb and find the stone rolled away. A young man tells them Jesus has risen, and they flee in fear.

stories.title: The Births of John and Jesus
stories.summary: Gabriel announces John's birth to Zechariah and Jesus's birth to Mary. Mary visits Elizabeth, John is born, and Jesus is born in Bethlehem and visited by shepherds.

stories.title: Presentation and the Boy Jesus in the Temple
stories.summary: Simeon and Anna see the infant Jesus at the temple. At twelve, Jesus stays behind in Jerusalem and is found among the teachers.

stories.title: Rejection at Nazareth
stories.summary: Jesus reads from Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue and says it is fulfilled. The crowd turns on him and tries to throw him off a cliff.

stories.title: The Miraculous Catch
stories.summary: After a night of fishing without success, Simon lets down his nets at Jesus's word and catches so many fish that the boats begin to sink. He leaves everything to follow Jesus.

stories.title: The Centurion and the Widow's Son
stories.summary: Jesus heals a centurion's servant at a distance and raises the only son of a widow at Nain.

stories.title: The Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus
stories.summary: At a Pharisee's house a woman bathes Jesus's feet with tears and oil. He tells a parable about two debtors and forgives her.

stories.title: The Good Samaritan and Mary and Martha
stories.summary: Asked who his neighbor is, Jesus tells of a Samaritan who helps a beaten traveler. He is then welcomed by Martha, while Mary sits at his feet.

stories.title: The Lost Sheep, Coin and Son
stories.summary: Jesus tells three parables of recovery: the lost sheep, the lost coin and the prodigal son with his elder brother.

stories.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
stories.summary: Jesus tells of a rich man and a poor man named Lazarus whose fortunes reverse after death.

stories.title: Zacchaeus
stories.summary: The tax collector Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus, welcomes him to his house, and promises to repay those he cheated.

stories.title: The Road to Emmaus
stories.summary: Two disciples walking to Emmaus meet the risen Jesus without recognizing him. They recognize him when he breaks bread and return to Jerusalem.

stories.title: The Ascension
stories.summary: Jesus appears to the disciples, opens the scriptures to them, and is carried up into heaven as he blesses them.

stories.title: The First Disciples and the Wedding at Cana
stories.summary: Andrew and another disciple follow Jesus, and Philip and Nathanael join them. At a wedding in Cana Jesus turns water into wine.

stories.title: Cleansing the Temple and Nicodemus
stories.summary: Jesus drives merchants from the temple at Passover. Nicodemus visits by night and hears that one must be born again.

stories.title: The Woman at the Well
stories.summary: Jesus asks a Samaritan woman for water and speaks of living water. Many Samaritans in her town believe.

stories.title: Healing at Bethesda
stories.summary: Jesus heals a man who had been ill thirty-eight years at the pool of Bethesda on a Sabbath. He then speaks of his relationship to the Father.

stories.title: Bread of Life
stories.summary: Jesus feeds the five thousand, walks on the sea, and teaches in Capernaum that he is the bread of life. Many disciples leave him.

stories.title: The Woman Caught in Adultery
stories.summary: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery and ask whether she should be stoned. Jesus tells the one without sin to throw the first stone, and he sends her away.

stories.title: The Man Born Blind
stories.summary: Jesus gives sight to a man born blind. The Pharisees question him and his parents and cast the man out.

stories.title: Jesus at the Feast of Dedication
stories.summary: At the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, Jesus is asked whether he is the Christ. Some take up stones after his answer and try to seize him, but he escapes and goes beyond Jordan, where many believe in him.

stories.title: The Raising of Lazarus
stories.summary: Jesus raises Lazarus of Bethany after four days in the tomb. The council then resolves to put Jesus to death.

stories.title: Anointing and Triumphal Entry
stories.summary: Mary anoints Jesus six days before Passover. He enters Jerusalem on a donkey, and some Greeks ask to see him.

stories.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
stories.summary: During supper Jesus washes his disciples’ feet and tells them to serve one another. He identifies his betrayer with a morsel given to Judas, who leaves, and foretells that Peter will deny him three times.

stories.title: Arrest, Trial and Crucifixion
stories.summary: Jesus is arrested in a garden, questioned by Annas and Pilate, crucified, and buried by Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus.

stories.title: The Resurrection Appearances
stories.summary: Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty and sees the risen Jesus. He appears to the disciples, and Thomas believes after seeing his wounds.

stories.title: Breakfast by the Sea of Tiberias
stories.summary: Jesus appears to seven disciples after a night of fishing, eats with them, and asks Peter three times whether he loves him.

stories.title: The Ascension and the Replacement of Judas
stories.summary: Jesus is taken up after promising the Holy Spirit. The apostles choose Matthias by lot to replace Judas.

stories.title: Pentecost
stories.summary: The Spirit comes on the believers, who speak in other languages. Peter preaches, about three thousand are baptized, and the community shares its goods.

stories.title: The Lame Man Healed and Arrest of Peter and John
stories.summary: Peter and John heal a lame man at the temple gate. They are arrested, speak boldly before the council, and the believers pray for courage.

stories.title: Ananias and Sapphira
stories.summary: The believers share property, but Ananias and Sapphira lie about the price of a field and both die.

stories.title: Stephen
stories.summary: Seven men are chosen to serve the widows. Stephen is accused of blasphemy, gives a speech recounting Israel's history, and is stoned.

stories.title: Philip and the Ethiopian
stories.summary: Persecution scatters the church. Philip preaches in Samaria and explains Isaiah to an Ethiopian official, whom he baptizes.

stories.title: Saul's Conversion
stories.summary: Saul, traveling to Damascus to arrest believers, is struck blind by a light from heaven. Ananias restores his sight, and Saul begins preaching Jesus.

stories.title: Peter, Cornelius and the Gentiles
stories.summary: Peter has a vision of unclean animals and is sent to the centurion Cornelius. The Spirit falls on the Gentile household, and the Jerusalem church accepts it.

stories.title: Peter's Escape and Herod's Death
stories.summary: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, whom an angel frees. Later the people acclaim Herod’s speech as the voice of a god; he is struck by an angel because he does not give God the glory, and dies.

stories.title: Paul's First Journey
stories.summary: Barnabas and Saul are sent out from Antioch. They preach in Cyprus, Pisidian Antioch and Lystra, where Paul is stoned, and return to appoint elders.

stories.title: The Jerusalem Council
stories.summary: The apostles and elders meet to decide whether Gentile believers must be circumcised. They send a letter asking only a few things of them.

stories.title: Paul in Philippi
stories.summary: Timothy joins Paul, who is called to Macedonia. In Philippi Lydia believes, and Paul and Silas are imprisoned. An earthquake opens the prison doors, the jailer is baptized, and the magistrates order their release the next day.

stories.title: Thessalonica, Athens and Corinth
stories.summary: Paul preaches in Thessalonica and Berea, speaks to the Areopagus in Athens, and spends eighteen months in Corinth.

stories.title: Ephesus
stories.summary: Paul teaches in Ephesus for about two years. A riot led by silversmiths follows, and he later raises Eutychus at Troas and bids the Ephesian elders farewell.

stories.title: Paul Arrested in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Paul goes to Jerusalem, is seized in the temple, addresses the crowd, and is brought before the council. A plot against him leads to transfer to Caesarea.

stories.title: Paul Before Felix, Festus and Agrippa
stories.summary: Paul defends himself before Felix, Festus and King Agrippa, and appeals to Caesar.

stories.title: Shipwreck and Rome
stories.summary: Paul sails for Rome, survives a storm and shipwreck at Malta, and arrives to preach under house arrest.
